rules.title: Welcome, Operative
rules.front:
SETUP
1. Read today's Intro Card.
2. Shuffle today's 3 player cards into your 12-card Operative Deck (15 cards). Draw 4.
3. Shuffle today's Threat Cards into the Threat Deck. Deal 3 face-up in a row: the Scene Row.
4. Set the Lead and Exposure markers to the Intro Card's starting values.

GOAL: Reach today's Lead target before your cover is blown.
rules.back:
YOUR CARDS
Each card shows a suit and a Power value:
RECON  ·  STEALTH  ·  FORCE

THREATS
Each Threat shows a requirement, like  STEALTH x2 + 5:
- 2 symbols of its preferred suit (some Threats list an alternate suit that also counts)
- at least 5 total Power
It also shows its Reward, Clean bonus, and any Pressure or timer.

rules.title: Your Turn: Play 2 Cards
rules.front:
Every turn has 3 steps: Play 2 Cards, Pressure, Draw 2.

STEP 1: PLAY EXACTLY 2 CARDS
Use each card one of two ways:
- TUCK it under a Threat whose preferred or alternate suit matches. It adds 1 symbol of its suit and its Power.
- USE ITS ABILITY (the text box) instead, then discard it.

Cards stay under a Threat across turns until it is cleared, so you can wear down a big Threat over several turns.
rules.back:
CLEARING A THREAT
When the symbols and Power under a Threat meet its requirement, it is cleared:
- Claim its Reward.
- Discard it and the cards under it.
- Deal a new Threat into the empty slot.

CLEAN CLEAR
If every card under it is its preferred suit, and its preferred-suit symbols (cards and Allies) meet the requirement on their own, also gain its Clean bonus.

rules.title: Pressure & Drawing
rules.front:
STEP 2: PRESSURE
Every Threat still in the Scene Row applies its Pressure (for example, +1 Exposure).

TIMERS: When a Threat with a timer enters the Scene Row, place a die on it showing that number. Turn it down by 1 each Pressure step. At 0 the Threat escapes: apply its Expiry effect, discard it, and deal a new Threat.

STEP 3: DRAW 2
Draw 2 cards. Your hand stays at 4 until your deck runs out.
rules.back:
THE EPISODE ENDS when:
- your Lead reaches today's target, or
- your Exposure hits the redline (6), or
- your deck and hand are both empty, or
- the Scene Row and Threat Deck are both empty (gain +1 Lead first).

STARS (0 to 3)
• Reached the Lead target
• Exposure at or below today's threshold
• Completed today's Bonus Objective

rules.title: After the Episode
rules.front:
1. Gather all 15 of your player cards.
2. DISCARD DOWN TO 12: choose 3 cards to retire—any cards, even today's new ones. Retired cards go back into the pack (or box slot) named on them. This is how you shape your deck.
3. Put today's Intro, Rule, Threat, and Outro Cards back in today's pack.
4. Record your Stars on the campaign sheet.
rules.back:
QUICK REFERENCE
Turn: Play 2 · Pressure · Draw 2
Tuck: +1 symbol of the card's suit, + its Power
Clean Clear: only the preferred suit counted
Timer at 0: Threat escapes, apply Expiry
End: Lead target · redline · out of cards · Scene Cleared
After: discard down to 12

rules.title: Gear
rules.front:
GEAR
Gear cards are equipment. Playing one counts as one of your 2 plays. Place it on the table: it stays in play for the rest of the episode, and its ongoing ability works every turn.

Gear has no Power and can't be tucked under Threats.
rules.back:
ALLIES
Allies are contacts and assets. Playing one counts as one of your 2 plays. Place it on the table: it stays in play.

An Ally's suit symbols count toward EVERY Threat you engage while it's in play—as if a card of that suit were tucked under each one.

Allies have no Power.

rules.title: Ally Cover
rules.front:
ALLY COVER
During Pressure, before any one Pressure or Expiry effect resolves, you may defeat one of your Allies in play to cancel that effect. Move the Ally to your discard pile.

Defeat lasts only for this episode: the Ally is back in your deck next time.
rules.back:
TIP
Allies make big Threats easier and protect you when things go wrong. Deciding when to spend one is often the key choice of an episode.

Gear and Allies return to your deck after every episode like any other card, and you can retire them in the end-of-day cut.

rules.title: Encrypted Threats
rules.front:
Some Threat cards have an ENCRYPTED back.

When an Encrypted Threat enters the Scene Row, it goes in FACE-DOWN. While face-down it has no Pressure and no timer, and you can't tuck cards under it. It just takes up its slot.

Encrypted Threats carry richer Rewards, so they're worth cracking.
rules.back:
DECRYPTING
Play any RECON card to a face-down Threat (one of your 2 plays) and flip it face-up. If it has a timer, place its die now.

If Recon is its preferred or alternate suit, your card stays under it and counts. Otherwise, discard the card.

The Master Decryptor perk lets any card decrypt.

rules.title: Memory Flashbacks
rules.front:
Today's pack holds a CONDITIONED CARD—one of your 3 new cards—and its AWAKENED CARD, set aside under a Flashback back. Don't read the Awakened Card yet.

Every flashback happens today: the Conditioned Card always awakens by the end of the episode.
rules.back:
AWAKENING DURING PLAY
The Conditioned Card prints a trigger. If its trigger is met when you play it, it awakens:
- Swap in the Awakened Card and play it instead.
- Gain its Awakening bonus.
- Read its flashback.

rules.title: Awakening at the End
rules.front: If the Conditioned Card hasn't awakened by the end of the episode—for any reason—it awakens during cleanup, before you discard down to 12. Read the flashback and swap in the Awakened Card (no bonus).
rules.back:
AFTER AWAKENING
The dormant card goes back in the pack. From now on, the Awakened Card is an ordinary player card—keep it, or retire it in the cut like any other.

rules.title: Pursuers
rules.front:
Today's Intro Card places a PURSUER in a 4th Scene Row slot. It is not part of the Threat Deck.

Neutralize it like any Threat—symbols and Power, cards stay under it—but it needs far more. Clearing it claims its Reward, and its slot stays empty.

Pursuers can't be Vanished. Some also print an ongoing effect.
rules.back:
HUNT & STRIKE
A Pursuer shows a HUNT number instead of a timer. Place a die on it set to that number and turn it down by 1 each Pressure step.

At 0 it STRIKES: apply its Strike effect, then reset the die to its Hunt number. Pursuers never escape.

Ally Cover can cancel a Strike. Stall works on its die. Scene Cleared requires the Pursuer to be neutralized.

rules.title: Black-Site Lockdown
rules.front:
TWO-PHASE THREATS are marked with a lock. Clearing one doesn't free its slot: claim its Reward as usual, then put its matching COUNTERMEASURE CARD (set aside during setup) into the same slot.

The Countermeasure is a Threat in every way. Clear it to finish the job.
rules.back:
SETUP REMINDER
During setup, set aside today's Countermeasure Cards (Countermeasure back) without reading them. Each names the Two-Phase Threat it follows.

If a Two-Phase Threat escapes or is swapped away, its Countermeasure never appears.

rules.title: Clearance Perks (prototype)
rules.front:
PROTOTYPE NOTE
In the full game, Outro Cards unlock Clearance Perks on Days 3, 7, 10, 13, 17, 20, and 24. For jump-in days, check the perks listed on the Jump-In Card on your campaign sheet.

Each unlocked perk can be used ONCE PER EPISODE. Mark its "used" box when you use it; erase the marks during cleanup.
rules.back:
PROTOTYPE NOTE
JUMP-IN CARDS set you up as if you'd played the earlier days:
1. Build your 12-card deck from the cards listed (PROTO cards stand in for cards from days not yet written).
2. Check the listed perks on your sheet.
3. Then set up the day normally.
